P1group.Title: Appeals against conviction or sentence, etc.

P2para.Text: Subject to this Article, a person convicted by a magistrates' court may appeal to a county court,—

P3para.Text: whether or not he pleaded guilty, against his sentence;
if he did not plead guilty, against the conviction.

Text.Addition: Article 6 of the Criminal Justice (Northern Ireland) Order 1996 (under which a conviction of an offence for which an order for conditional or absolute discharge is made is deemed not to be a conviction except for certain purposes) shall not prevent an appeal under this Article, whether against conviction or otherwise.

P2para.Text: In paragraph (1) “sentence” includes any order passed on the person for the offence, whether on conviction or in subsequent proceedings, not being—

Para.Text: an order for the payment of costs; or
any other order subject to a restriction referred to in paragraph 9(1)(b) of Schedule 5.

Text.Addition: A person may appeal to a county court against—
a fine imposed under paragraph (a), or an order made under paragraph (b) or (c), of paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Criminal Justice (Northern Ireland) Order 1996 (N.I. 24);
the dismissal of an application under Part 3 or 4 of that Schedule;
a fine imposed, or an order made, under Article 41(2) or
of the Criminal Justice (Children) (Northern Ireland) Order 1998 (N.I. 9);
an order made under paragraph 3 of Schedule 1A to that Order; or
the dismissal of an application under paragraph 5 of that Schedule (otherwise than to the Crown Court) to make an order under sub-paragraph (1) of that paragraph.

P2para.Text: A person ordered under Article 7(1) of the Criminal Justice (Northern Ireland) Order 1996 to give good security for the good behaviour of an offender may appeal to the county court.
